policy.patch: 0.x.y contains compatible fixes and narrowly necessary tests/documentation. A bug label or migration alone does not settle compatibility.
policy.priority_legend: P1: consequential security/integrity or required production evidence; P2: moderate affected-workflow risk; P3: later improvement. Priority is assessed here, not a GitHub label or a release-necessity score.
policy.size_legend: S: bounded surface; M: several paths or a race; L: cross-layer/client/deployment work. These are planning estimates, not day commitments.

standing_rules: Every PR that changes a 0.5.1 issue updates release-data.json, appends a row to execution.md and re-runs render.py in the same PR.
Every PR keeps docstring coverage at or above 80% for the functions in each file it creates or edits, counted before the first push.
Run refresh.py before render.py whenever GitHub milestones or issue states have changed. refresh.py reads GitHub only and never writes to it.

items.title: Code that coverage proved nothing can reach
items.fit: Compatible removal of unreachable code, or a comment that keeps it as a deliberate guard.
items.next_action: Draft a keep or delete proposal per item on the issue; the maintainer decides each one before any code moves.

items.title: ADR-0019 does not list the Resolve() validation refusal as a dead-letter cause
items.next_action: Review factual correction separately; defer behavior decisions unless production label scope needs them.

items.title: Subprocess test helpers read stdout before stderr and deadlock on more than 64 KB of stderr
items.next_action: Recover 31b3439c/72fdffef without replacing them; migrate only callers required by upcoming validation first.

items.title: Consume stores any integer recipe_id, including negative ids and ids no recipe has
items.fit: Compatible fix: invalid input is refused, valid input is unchanged.

items.title: prose-baseline-prune fails daily: it pushes to master, which requires a pull request
items.next_action: Merge PR #1012, enable 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests', then run the workflow by hand once.

items.title: Calendar API 500 includes the user-supplied event title in its body
items.fit: Low-severity disclosure fix: the response body changes only on the error path.
items.next_action: Decide whether the 500 body may carry the title; otherwise log it server-side.

items.title: Uploading a userfile under an existing unreferenced name reveals that the name exists
items.fit: Low-severity disclosure fix: needs the ADR-0048 item 9 decision first.
items.next_action: Decide whether the existence signal matters; update ADR-0048 item 9.

items.title: Backup/restore drill against the v0.5.0 artifacts (release gate R5)
items.fit: Verification and documentation only: closes release gate R5.
items.next_action: Run the documented dump and restore against the v0.5.0 images on a disposable database and record the report.

milestones.description: Later feature release: OAuth then federation; installation country, canonical/scoped barcode resolution and web onboarding, each behind its own design/ADR gates. Full API audit remains later work. These are not requirements for 0.5.0.
Follow-ups found while building 0.5.0 that do not block the first production release: presentation residuals, low-severity disclosures and CI hygiene. Lands after 0.5.0 and before 0.6.0.
